Prior distribution of the between-site standard deviation

Source: R/class-sd-prior.R
sd_prior.Rd

Specifies the prior of sigma_tau for reliability_posterior(): the flat prior of Lee (2026), which is the default, or a half-normal, half-t, half-Cauchy or uniform prior.

Usage

sd_prior(
  type = c("flat", "half_normal", "half_t", "half_cauchy", "uniform"),
  scale = NULL,
  df = NULL,
  upper = NULL
)

Arguments

type

Family of the prior: one of "flat" (the default), "half_normal", "half_t", "half_cauchy" or "uniform".

scale

Scale of a half-normal, half-t or half-Cauchy prior, a positive number in the units of the estimates. It has no default, because a sensible scale depends on the scale of the effects.

df

Degrees of freedom of a half-t prior, a positive number.

upper

Upper limit of a uniform prior, a positive number.

Value

An object of class sd_prior, a list with the components

  • type: the family.

  • scale, df or upper: the parameters that the family uses.

  • tail: the power \(k\) with which the density falls off in its upper tail, which decides which posterior moments exist: 0 for the flat prior, df + 1 for the half-t, 2 for the half-Cauchy and Inf for the half-normal and uniform priors.

Details

Proper SD priors are an experimental extension beyond Lee (2026); their interfaces may change in a later 0.x release.

The flat prior is uniform on the mean of the effects and on sigma_tau (not on sigma_tau^2). Under it the posterior is proper only with at least 3 sites, and the posterior mean of \(\sigma_\tau^{q}\) exists only with more than \(q + 2\) sites; so with 3 or 4 sites the posterior mean of sigma_tau^2 does not exist, although those of the bounded diagnostics do. With a mean model of \(p\) columns, the condition is \(J > q + p + 1\).

A prior whose density falls off like \(\sigma^{-k}\) lowers the bound by \(k\): the moment of order \(q\) exists when \(J > q + p + 1 - k\), with \(k = \nu + 1\) for a half-t prior with \(\nu\) degrees of freedom and \(k = 2\) for the half-Cauchy. Every moment exists under the half-normal and the uniform priors. Every prior other than the flat one needs at least \(p + 1\) sites.

With few sites the flat prior can matter, as for any prior on a variance parameter (Gelman, 2006); prior_sensitivity() compares the summaries under several priors.

References

Gelman, A. (2006). Prior distributions for variance parameters in hierarchical models (comment on article by Browne and Draper). Bayesian Analysis, 1(3), 515-534. doi:10.1214/06-BA117A

Lee, J. (2026). The geometry of informativeness: A Bregman-centroid diagnostic for partial pooling in multisite trials. Unpublished manuscript.

See also

prior_sensitivity() to compare the summaries under several priors, and vignette("posterior-summaries") for the choice of prior.

Examples

sd_prior()
#> Prior: flat on the mean and on sigma_tau
sd_prior("half_normal", scale = 0.5)
#> Prior: half-normal on sigma_tau with scale 0.5, flat on the mean
sd_prior("half_t", scale = 0.5, df = 3)
#> Prior: half-t on sigma_tau with scale 0.5 and 3 degrees of freedom, flat on the mean
